newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bank lending fell 0.2 pct in January - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan bank lending fell 0.2 pct in January - BOJ.

text.p: The average balance of bank lending by Japan's 149 banks dipped 0.2 percent in January from a year ago to 534.36 trillion yen, the fourth month in a row of year-on-year declines, the Bank of Japan (BOJ) said on Friday.
The decline in lending reflected efforts by Japanese banks to eliminate non-performing loans from their balance sheets, financial sources said.

The pace of the decline slowed, however, from the 0.5 percent year-on-year drop in both October and November and the 0.4 percent fall in December, as corporate demand for lending has gradually been picking up, they said.
The average loan balance at Japan's 10 big commercial banks was up 0.5 percent at a total of 246.71 trillion yen in January, the BOJ said in a report.
The lending balance for three long-term credit banks fell 2.8 percent to 45.54 trillion yen, while seven major trust banks recorded a drop of 5.0 percent to 53.23 trillion yen.

The lending balance for foreign banks operating in Japan rose 10.7 percent in January to 5.83 trillion yen, as foreign banks bought loans through loan participation programmes from Japanese banks trying to cut their assets, the sources said.
